title: An Experimental System to Study Mechanotransduction in Fetal Lung Cells
protocol: Mix 120 μg of laminin with 12 ml of cold sterile 1X PBS per plate.
Add 2 ml of the solution to each well of Bioflex untreated plates (final concentration of laminin is 2 μg/cm²).
Wrap the plates with plastic and place at 4°C on a flat surface overnight.
Wash the wells 3 times with 1X PBS under sterile conditions the next day.
Add 1 ml of 1% BSA in 1X PBS to each well and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour to block non-specific binding sites.
Rinse the plates 3 times with 1X PBS to remove unadsorbed proteins.
Keep the plates at 37°C in DMEM until cells are isolated from step 2.14.
Have screen cups with different size nylon meshes autoclaved and ready the day before isolation.
Obtain fetal lungs from timed-pregnant mouse/rat on E17-19 of gestation.
Transfer the tissue into a 50 ml conical tube containing DMEM medium.
Place the tube on ice.
Make digestion buffer in a 50 ml conical tube: Mix 8.5 ml DMEM, 0.5 ml 500 mM pH 7.4 HEPES, 5 mg Collagenase 1, 5 mg Collagenase 1A, and 1 ml chicken serum, heat inactivated.
Filter the mixture through a 0.2 micron syringe filter inside the sterile hood.
Place the conical tube containing the digestion buffer in a water bath at 37°C.
Remove DMEM medium from the tissue-containing conical tube and transfer the lung tissue into a sterile Petri dish.
Mince the lungs well with sterile scissors or razor blade to make tissue pieces less than 1 mm.
Transfer minced lung tissue into the pre-warmed digestion buffer.
Digest the tissue by pipetting up and down 100 times with a 10 ml pipette, then 100 times with a 5 ml pipette, and finally 100 times with a Pasteur pipette.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 1,300 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Re-suspend the pellet containing the cells in 15 ml of DMEM plus 20% FBS.
Take out screen cups with 100-, 30-, and 15-micron nylon meshes and place them on sterile 150 ml beakers.
Add cell homogenate to the first mesh cup (100 microns).
Filter through each subsequent mesh cup sequentially, starting from 100- micron, then 30-micron, and finally 15-micron mesh screens.
Collect clumped non-filtered cells from the 30- and 15-micron meshes after several washes with DMEM plus 10% FBS to facilitate the filtration of non-epithelial cells.
Discard the filtrate from the 15-micron mesh.
Incubate cells from step 2.11 in 75-cm² flasks for 30 minutes.
Collect the supernatant and centrifuge at 1,300 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Resuspend the pellet containing the cells in serum-free DMEM.
Plate the cell suspension on Bioflex six-well plates precoated with laminin or fibronectin to achieve between 60-70% confluency the following day.
Take the filtrate from the 15-micron mesh without previous washing and plate onto 75-cm² flasks at 37°C for 30-60 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant after adherence of fibroblasts.
Replace with serum-free DMEM and incubate overnight.
Harvest cells with 0.25% (wt/vol) trypsin in 0.4 mM EDTA the next day.
Plate harvested cells on Bioflex plates precoated with fibronectin.
Seed cells (around 50% confluent) on Bioflex culture plates in serum-free DMEM (2 ml/well).
Allow cells to attach and spread for at least 6 hours before experiments.
Maintain cells in culture for around 24 hours before applying mechanical strain.
Trypsinize, count, and seed cells the day after isolation if a specific number of cells is required.
Replace media with fresh serum-free DMEM (2 ml/well) the next day.
Mount Bioflex plates in a Flexcell FX-5000 Strain Unit.
Ensure monolayers are no greater than 80% confluent before initiating experiments.
Apply equibiaxial strain to the membranes according to the regimen simulating mechanical forces in vivo.
Culture cells on non-stretched membranes as controls for comparison.
Process monolayers at the end of experiments for analysis by real-time PCR, Western blot, or other methods.
Fix monolayers for immunocytochemistry after cutting silastic membranes from plates and mounting them on glass slides using water as a mounting agent.
Use supernatant to investigate growth factors, cytokines, and other substances.
